items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo gets defensive boost as Al Nassr recover Mohamed Simakan ahead of Al Diriyah clash
items.description:
Al Nassr received a timely boost in defense ahead of their next Saudi Pro League match, as Mohamed Simakan is back in contention to face Al Diriyah. The French center back had been a doubt after suffering a muscle strain, but he has now passed the team's fitness tests, which should give Ange Postecoglou some […] 
Al Nassr received a timely boost in defense ahead of their next Saudi Pro League match, as Mohamed Simakan is back in contention to face Al Diriyah. The French center back had been a doubt after suffering a muscle strain, but he has now passed the team’s fitness tests, which should give Ange Postecoglou some relief as Cristiano Ronaldo and company return to league action on Friday, October 9.



According to Saudi newspaper Arriyadiyah, Simakan took part in the full team training session on Thursday, the day before the match, and has entered Postecoglou’s plans. 



His recovery could have been a real problem for the coach, since the doubts about his fitness threatened to leave Al Nassr short in defense, but the Frenchman’s return gives the team a key piece at a moment when it needs stability at the back.



The match against Al Diriyah, scheduled for 2 p.m. ET, comes at an important point for Al Nassr in the standings. The club sits third in the Saudi Pro League with 16 points, two behind leaders Al Hilal and one behind Al Ittihad, who occupy second place with 17.




Friday night. AlAwwal Park. You know where to be 💛🏟️ pic.twitter.com/EhVXvzFPH5— AlNassr FC (@AlNassrFC_EN) October 8, 2026




Postecoglou’s side is also coming off a 4-0 loss to Al Ain in its last outing, so a solid defensive performance against a newly promoted side would help them turn the page. The game also marks Ronaldo’s return to club action following a turbulent international break with Portugal, which ended with the forward leaving the national team camp.


        


Several other absences force changes for Al Nassr



Simakan’s return comes with some bad news for Postecoglou, as Abdulelah Al-Amri has been left out of the squad due to fatigue after winning the Gulf Cup with Saudi Arabia, while Abdulrahman Ghareeb has also been excluded because he is not physically ready to play, according to Arriyadiyah.



The club will also be short in goal, so Postecoglou has called up young goalkeeper Abdulhadi Al-Alwan to cover for the injuries to Nawaf Al-Aqidi, Raghad Al-Najjar and Mubarak Al-Buainain.



Nawaf Boushal, Abdullah Al-Khaibari and Abdullah Al-Hamdan, who also won the Gulf Cup with Saudi Arabia, arrived at the club’s headquarters alongside Al-Amri, though the report does not specify their status for the match.

items.title: Christian Pulisic’s role for Milan’s clash vs Sassuolo takes intriguing turn as Ruben Amorim’s lineup begins to emerge ahead of packed October
items.description:
Battered by injuries and facing a relentless fixture list, the Rossoneri mastermind is on the precipice of a profound tactical metamorphosis, where the role of the American talisman hangs delicately in the balance. 
A veil of intrigue surrounds Christian Pulisic as Milan braces for a looming battle against Sassuolo. With the international break in the rearview mirror, Ruben Amorim must forge a path through a grueling, unforgiving October gauntlet. Battered by injuries and facing a relentless fixture list, the Rossoneri mastermind is on the precipice of a profound tactical metamorphosis, where the role of the American talisman hangs delicately in the balance.



Milan has started the league campaign strongly under Amorim, collecting three wins and two draws from its opening five Serie A matches. The victory over Lecce before the break was particularly encouraging, with Pulisic, Diego Moreira and Adrien Rabiot all finding the net in a convincing 3-0 win.



The Rossoneri now return to action on Sunday, October 11, against Sassuolo at the Mapei Stadium. The match begins an extremely demanding month in which the Rossoneri are expected to play for 21 points across just 28 days, making squad rotation increasingly important.



Amorim has already shown that he wants his side to evolve tactically, and this weekend could provide another example. The Portuguese coach is reportedly considering a more attacking setup while still trying to maintain enough defensive balance to deal with Sassuolo’s counter-attacking threat.



CHRISTIAN PULISIC! ⚽#MilanLecce 1-0 pic.twitter.com/asefBjFFWe— Lega Serie A (@SerieA_EN) September 20, 2026 



Injuries could force Milan into tactical change



Milan will be without Alexis Saelemaekers, while Pervis Estupinan remains a fitness doubt after missing time with injury. Both players have been important options, leaving Amorim with decisions to make on the flanks. According to Gazzetta dello Sport, the circumstances could lead Amorim to field “his most attacking side ever”. 



The coach has generally avoided using two pure attacking wingers from the start, but the current selection problems could encourage him to take a different approach. The Neroverdi should provide a stern test for any tactical experiment. The hosts have already shown they can cause problems for stronger opponents, including a victory over Juventus.



AC Milan coach Ruben Amorim gestures



Will Pulisic play against Sassuolo and what role?



Amid the tactical uncertainty, Christian Pulisic is expected to start behind Goncalo Ramos if Amorim switches to a 4-2-3-1 formation. The American would operate as the central attacking midfielder, with Ramos leading the line and another attacking player occupying the wide left position.



That would represent a slight change from the alternative 3-4-2-1 system, in which Pulisic has also been projected to start alongside another attacking midfielder behind Ramos. Either way, the supplied lineup reports agree on one important point: the American remains one of the key attacking pieces in the coach’s plans.



How Milan could line up against Sassuolo as per La Gazzetta dello Sport



A possible 4-2-3-1 would feature Mike Maignan in goal, with Mario Gila and Strahinja Pavlovic involved in the defensive line and Davide Bartesaghi potentially replacing Estupinan. Samuel Chukwueze, Luka Modric and Adrien Rabiot would provide the midfield structure, while Pulisic would sit behind Ramos.



The 28-year-old forward could also benefit from the form of the players around him. Goncalo Ramos returned from international duty with three goals in four appearances for Portugal, while Alphadjo Cisse also scored for Italy Under-21.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s mother sends warning to Portugal in defence of her son’s legacy as Jorge Jesus rift continues
items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo's departure from the Portugal national team has taken an emotional turn following public comments from his mother, Maria Dolores Aveiro. 
The circumstances surrounding Cristiano Ronaldo’s sudden exit from the Portugal national team have evolved following recent public statements from his mother, Maria Dolores Aveiro. In a television interview, she addressed the ongoing fallout resulting from her son’s dispute with manager Jorge Jesus. These comments arrive at a highly sensitive juncture for the 41-year-old forward, whose abrupt exit from the training camp has generated significant scrutiny regarding his continued involvement in international soccer.



The episode has already produced a disciplinary case and a public explanation from Ronaldo, who apologized for his actions while insisting that he remains available to represent Portugal. Now, his mother has offered her own perspective on how the situation has affected the family and how she believes her son’s extraordinary contribution should be viewed.



Dolores Aveiro admitted that Ronaldo’s departure from the Portugal camp was extremely difficult for her to process. Speaking to TV 7 Dias, she described the episode as a shock and revealed that she became emotional after learning that her son had left the squad.



“I feel sad, and that’s natural. It was a shock. My son could have left through the front door, but he left through the back door. But it’s okay; God will take care of everything. I cried a little. Sometimes crying is good to help us release what we’re feeling. We have to get through this phase.”



Cristiano Ronaldo #7 of Portugal reacts



She also revealed that she called Ronaldo shortly after he left the camp. According to Dolores, her son tried to reassure her that he would eventually explain his side of the story, while she encouraged him to remain calm during the difficult period.



Dolores Aveiro delivers her strongest message



The most striking part of Dolores’ comments was her defense of Ronaldo’s place in Portuguese football history. She believes her son has given enormous amounts to the national team and feels that his contribution has not received the recognition she believes it deserves.



“Cristiano has given so much to Portugal, and he will always be there. He has always been Portugal’s hero, but they don’t give him the recognition he deserves. They don’t appreciate Cristiano the way they should. This is the Portuguese we have.”



Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal holds the UEFA Nations League trophy 



The comments add another emotional layer to a dispute that has already become one of the biggest stories surrounding the national team. Dolores’ words suggest that, from the Ronaldo family’s perspective, the issue extends beyond one disagreement over playing time and touches on how the captain’s legacy is being treated.



Ronaldo’s legacy now part of the debate



The disagreement with Jesus has inevitably shifted attention toward the final stage of Ronaldo’s Portugal career. At 41, he remains the national team’s all-time leading scorer and one of the defining figures in its history, while his international career already includes the 2016 European Championship and more than two decades of service.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal holds the Euro 2016 trophy



For Dolores, that history should carry considerable weight when Ronaldo’s treatment is discussed. Her emotional intervention reflects the frustration within the player’s family, while Borges’ comments show that even those outside the immediate dispute continue to view Ronaldo’s legacy as something far bigger than one difficult international window.



Whether Ronaldo and Jesus can repair their relationship remains uncertain. For now, though, Ronaldo has left the door open to Portugal, his mother has made clear how strongly she feels about his treatment, and the debate over how one of the country’s greatest-ever players should be remembered has only intensified.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s entourage reportedly delivered major ultimatum to Jorge Jesus as Portugal crisis takes another turn
items.description:
A close friend of Jesus claims that Ronaldo's entourage made a major demand during the dispute, putting further pressure on a relationship that had already deteriorated over playing-time promises. 
The Cristiano Ronaldo and Jorge Jesus feud is completely blowing up with a massive new allegation. A close friend of Jesus claims that Ronaldo’s entourage made a major demand during the dispute, putting further pressure on a relationship that had already deteriorated over playing-time promises.



The allegation was made by Carlos Padrao, a former goalkeeper and close associate of Jesus, during an appearance on SIC Notícias’ Jogo Aberto. According to Padrao, Tiago Craveiro, a strategic consultant for Ronaldo’s company CR7 SA, contacted someone within Jesus’ circle as the disagreement intensified.



The controversy started during Portugal‘s UEFA Nations League campaign in September. Ronaldo had reportedly agreed to a plan regarding his playing time, but he was left on the bench against Norway on September 27 despite being told he would feature for around 30 minutes.



The 41-year-old warmed up during the second half but was never introduced as the Selecao won 2-1. Ronaldo subsequently accused Jesus of breaking his word and later explained that the dispute was about trust rather than a demand to play every match.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal.



Ronaldo then left Portugal’s training camp before the next fixture and released a lengthy statement explaining his decision. He claimed that Jesus had broken two separate agreements, including a later understanding about how the coach would publicly explain the situation.



Ronaldo’s entourage allegedly issued stark ultimatum



That dispute has now produced an even more serious allegation. Padrao claims that Craveiro threatened that Jesus would be dismissed unless he publicly apologized to Ronaldo, with the alleged demand being delivered through someone close to the coach rather than directly to Jesus.



According to Padrao, Ronaldo’s camp even attempted to prepare a specific script for the Portugal coach to read at the beginning of a press conference. “They tried to create a script for Jorge Jesus to apologize to Cristiano Ronaldo,” Padrao told SIC Notícias.



The experienced boss reportedly refused to follow the script or issue the requested formal apology. Instead, he acknowledged that his handling of Ronaldo’s warm-up against Norway had been a mistake while maintaining a distinction between admitting an error and apologizing.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal.



“Admitting a mistake is one thing, apologizing is another,” Padrao said, describing Jesus’ position. He also claimed that the coach is deeply saddened by the entire episode and remains affected by the deterioration of his relationship with Ronaldo.



Jesus previously had strong relationship with Ronaldo



The situation is particularly striking because Jesus and Ronaldo had recently worked together at Al-Nassr. The pair won the Saudi Pro League title together, and their relationship appeared to be strong before Jesus was appointed Portugal coach following the 2026 World Cup.



Cristiano Ronaldo and Jorge Jesus



Padrao has suggested that Jesus believed he could manage Ronaldo’s playing time precisely because of their previous relationship. The coach had also reportedly played a role in persuading Ronaldo to continue his international career after Portugal’s World Cup elimination by Spain.



That history makes the current disagreement more complicated. According to Padrao, Jesus never intended to create a confrontation with Ronaldo, and his friend believes the coach remains deeply disappointed that their relationship has reached this point.

items.title: Vinicius Junior’s market value takes another hit as struggles mount for Real Madrid and Brazil
items.description:
Vinicius Junior is going through one of the most difficult stretches of his career, and the numbers are now starting to reflect it. Between a slow start to the season at Real Madrid and a quiet international break with Brazil, the forward has seen the criticism around his performances grow on both fronts, and Transfermarkt's […] 
Vinicius Junior is going through one of the most difficult stretches of his career, and the numbers are now starting to reflect it. Between a slow start to the season at Real Madrid and a quiet international break with Brazil, the forward has seen the criticism around his performances grow on both fronts, and Transfermarkt’s latest update has made that decline official by lowering his market value to its lowest point in nearly four years.



According to the latest update, Vinicius is now valued at €130 million, which is €10 million less than his previous valuation and a drop of €70 million from the €200 million he reached in October 2024, shortly after helping Real Madrid win the Champions League.



The reduction comes as the 26-year-old struggles to find his best level for both club and country. For Real Madrid, he has scored just one goal in eight matches this season, to go with three assists in 652 minutes, and the criticism intensified after the 2-1 derby defeat to Atlético Madrid, when Yan Diomandé replaced him before the hour mark and made an immediate impact.



With Brazil, the picture has not been much brighter: he converted a late penalty in the 4-2 win over Australia, but the performance was far from a standout one, and a week earlier he had a forgettable hour in the 1-1 draw in Townsville before being substituted.



Vinicius Jr. of Brazil. (Getty Images)



Even so, Vinicius continues to have the full backing of the people who coach him. Carlo Ancelotti said after the win over Australia that “Vini Jr. deserves my patience” and that, even when he is not at his best, “he can still make the difference“. José Mourinho has also kept him in the starting lineup at Madrid despite the criticism, and the club recently reinforced its confidence in the forward by extending his contract until 2032, only two months ago.


        


From €200 million to €130 million in two years



Vinícius’ valuation reached its peak at €200 million in October 2024, after a season in which he helped Real Madrid win the Champions League. His value has been falling gradually since mid-2025, and this is the lowest figure attached to his name since November 2022, when he stood at €120 million just before the World Cup in Qatar, although at that time his price was on the rise rather than in decline.



DateMarket valueNovember 2022€120 millionJune 2023€150 millionDecember 2023€150 millionJune 2024€180 millionOctober 2024€200 millionDecember 2024€200 millionJune 2025€170 millionOctober 2025€150 millionDecember 2025€150 millionJune 2026€140 millionOctober 2026€130 million



Vinícius’ poor run could also open the door for other attacking options at Real Madrid. Yan Diomandé’s valuation jumped from €90 million to €120 million, the biggest increase in LaLiga, while Arda Güler reached €100 million for the first time, and both are in a position to take advantage if the Brazilian’s struggles continue.

items.title: Inter Miami reportedly plan long-term future with Lionel Messi after Argentina retirement
items.description:
Since Lionel Messi arrived in 2023, Inter Miami have grown from a promising MLS franchise into the league's most valuable club. 
Inter Miami are already planning a long-term future with Lionel Messi that goes well beyond his current contract, according to reports. Now that the 39-year-old has retired from the Argentina national team, he is fully focused on the MLS, and the club’s ownership want to keep him tied to the franchise even after he stops playing, a vision that includes the possibility of him becoming a shareholder.



Messi’s contract with Inter Miami runs through the end of the 2028 MLS season, but the club’s leadership do not want that date to mark the end of the relationship. Jorge Mas, the team’s managing owner and CEO, considers that the project built around Messi requires an investment of between $70 million and $80 million per year, taking into account all the elements linked to the player.



Xavier Asensi, the club’s president of business operations, has also revealed that Inter Miami already contemplate the scenario after Messi’s retirement and the chance that he can become part of the club’s ownership group once he stops playing professionally. BBC Sport reported that his agreement already includes a pathway to receive a minority stake in the team after his playing career ends, and that Messi prefers the idea of owning a club to coaching one.



Even so, nothing has been signed yet: there is no confirmed agreement to extend Messi’s contract through 2030, a date that for now should be understood as a long-term horizon and not as a closed renewal. For the moment, Messi’s immediate focus will be on the field, with Inter Miami set to host DC United on Saturday, October 10, at Nu Stadium in the MLS regular season.



Lionel Messi celebrates a goal for Inter Miami. (Getty Images)



How Messi turned Inter Miami into MLS’s most valuable club



Since Lionel Messi arrived in July 2023, Inter Miami have gone from a young franchise with promise to the league’s biggest commercial force. The club was valued at around $600 million before his signing, and Forbes now puts that figure at $1.35 billion, making Inter Miami the most valuable team in MLS ahead of LAFC.


        


The growth has come with trophies as well: the 2023 Leagues Cup, the 2024 Supporters’ Shield and the 2025 MLS Cup, a 3-1 win over Vancouver in which Messi provided an assist.



That growth explains why Inter Miami want to keep him for as long as possible. Keeping Messi reportedly costs the club between $70 and $80 million a year, according to Mas, but the commercial return has so far outweighed that investment. With much of the club’s recent value tied to his presence, Inter Miami are reportedly working on a long-term plan that would keep him involved beyond his playing career, including a potential path to a shareholder role.

items.title: Carlo Ancelotti leads Luis de la Fuente and Zinedine Zidane among highest-paid national team coaches as Lionel Scaloni’s place raises eyebrows
items.description:
Yet, amidst the glittering fortunes of the top earners, a glaring anomaly remains: the shockingly modest standing of Argentina's Lionel Scaloni, whose monumental recent triumphs are scarcely reflected in his earthly reward. 
The financial hierarchy of international soccer has been laid bare, with Carlo Ancelotti sitting unchallenged upon the throne. The Brazil mastermind towers above his peers, vastly out-earning the likes of Luis de la Fuente and Zinedine Zidane in a stark display of the immense wealth gap dividing the world’s elite managers. Yet, amidst the glittering fortunes of the top earners, a glaring anomaly remains: the shockingly modest standing of Argentina’s Lionel Scaloni, whose monumental recent triumphs are scarcely reflected in his earthly reward.



Transfermarkt’s figures underline how dramatically international management has changed. National teams are increasingly prepared to offer salaries comparable to major club jobs, with federations securing famous coaches on long-term contracts as they chase World Cup success.



Ancelotti is the clear leader, earning a reported €10 million ($11.7 million) per year with Brazil. His contract runs through 2030, giving the five-time Champions League-winning coach a long-term project with one of soccer’s most demanding national teams.



Jurgen Klopp is second with Germany on €7 million ($8.2 million) annually, leaving him €3 million behind Ancelotti. Mauricio Pochettino follows in third with the United States on €6.8 million ($8 million), while Thomas Tuchel earns €6 million ($7 million) with England.



Carlo Ancelotti, Head Coach of Brazil.



The numbers show just how much federations are willing to spend on proven managers. Ancelotti’s reputation, Klopp’s success with Liverpool and Pochettino’s growing role within the United States setup have all translated into substantial international contracts.



The top 10 reveals a fascinating financial divide



Spain’s Luis de la Fuente occupies fifth place on €5 million ($5.9 million) per year, with his contract running until 2032. Portugal’s Jorge Jesus and Roberto Mancini of Italy are next on €4 million ($4.7 million) each.



Luis de la Fuente, Head Coach of Spain, lifts the World Cup trophy.



Zinedine Zidane is eighth on €3.6 million ($4.2 million) with France, followed by Xavi with the Netherlands on €3 million ($3.5 million). That leaves one of international soccer’s most successful recent coaches surprisingly close to the bottom of the top 10.



Scaloni’s ranking surprises



Lionel Scaloni is ranked 10th on €2.3 million ($2.7 million) per year with Argentina, according to the Transfermarkt figures. His reported salary is less than a quarter of Ancelotti’s and significantly below the earnings of several coaches whose teams have achieved less in recent international tournaments.



Transfermarkt’s highest-paid national team coaches 



The contrast becomes particularly striking when Scaloni’s trophy cabinet is considered. Argentina has won the 2021 Copa America, 2022 Finalissima, 2022 World Cup and 2024 Copa America under his leadership, while the national team also reached the 2026 World Cup final.



Scaloni initially took charge in 2018 with limited senior managerial experience, so his original contract reflected his status at the time. His extraordinary success subsequently changed his reputation, but the reported salary has apparently failed to catch up with his transformation into one of international soccer’s most decorated coaches.



Lionel Scaloni with the World Cup trophy



Scaloni could be due a major salary increase



The biggest question surrounding the ranking is whether the 48-year-old boss’ current contract reflects his actual value. A coach who has delivered four major senior trophies and reached another World Cup final, earning €2.3 million ($2.7 million), looks like an outlier, particularly when compared with managers earning several million more.



Scaloni’s contract is reportedly due to expire at the end of 2026, making his future an important issue for Argentina. If the AFA renews his deal, his extraordinary record could support a significant increase.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo watches closely as Al Nassr want to recover Mohamed Simakan for Al Diriyah clash
items.description:
Al Nassr are preparing for Friday's Saudi Pro League match against Al Diriyah with the return of Cristiano Ronaldo to club action and one defensive question mark still to be resolved. The reigning champions will visit Al-Awwal Park for Matchday 8, and coach Ange Postecoglou may have to wait until the last moment to define […] 
Al Nassr are preparing for Friday’s Saudi Pro League match against Al Diriyah with the return of Cristiano Ronaldo to club action and one defensive question mark still to be resolved. The reigning champions will visit Al-Awwal Park for Matchday 8, and coach Ange Postecoglou may have to wait until the last moment to define his lineup.



According to Al Nassr insider Abdulaziz Al-Asimi, the club’s medical staff are working to get French defender Mohamed Simakan ready for the match. His availability will reportedly be determined during training on the day of the game, which means Postecoglou will not know until Friday whether he can count on him.



Al Nassr’s training sessions are now at full strength after the players who were away on international duty returned to the squad. Postecoglou, who had spent two weeks preparing without his national team players, can now work with the complete group ahead of Friday’s match.



The coach also used his pre-match news conference on Wednesday, October 7, to give a positive update on Ronaldo, who returns to his club after a turbulent week with Portugal, saying that the forward is fully fit and ready to play.




Two more days. We’ve missed this ⏳💛 pic.twitter.com/HGRIQwKJzt— AlNassr FC (@AlNassrFC_EN) October 7, 2026




Al Nassr arrive at the match after a heavy 4-0 defeat to Al Ain in the AFC Champions League Elite on September 15, and they will look to return to winning ways in the league, where they sit third in the table with 16 points, two behind leaders Al Hilal and one behind second-placed Al Ittihad.


        


Cristiano Ronaldo chases the Saudi Pro League Golden Boot



Ronaldo returns to the league with some ground to make up in the scoring charts. The 41-year-old has scored three goals in the Saudi Pro League this season, against Al Riyadh, Al Taawoun, and Abha, a tally that leaves him tied for ninth place with 14 other players.



He is seven goals behind the leader, Al Ahli’s Ivan Toney, who has 10 in seven games, and also trails Neom’s Alexandre Lacazette, who has five, as well as six players who have four each, among them Al Ittihad’s George Ilenikhena, Steven Bergwijn, and Youssef En-Nesyri.



With his last goal, against Abha on September 9, he reached 979 for his career, which leaves him 21 short of the 1,000-goal milestone, and with Al Nassr’s busy schedule ahead he will have plenty of opportunities to close the distance on Toney and the rest of the leaders.

items.title: Lionel Scaloni drops big hint about his future with Argentina as Lionel Messi era ends
items.description:
Lionel Scaloni hints he will continue as Argentina coach after Lionel Messi's farewell, as talks reportedly advance on an extension through the 2030 World Cup. 
Lionel Messi‘s farewell was not the only big topic in Argentina’s camp this week. The future of coach Lionel Scaloni was also a constant subject, and he gave a new hint on Tuesday, October 6, after the 3-0 win over Benin that closed the Messi era with the national team.



Speaking at the post-match news conference, Scaloni first addressed how Argentina will replace its captain. “The only way to compensate is with a team. Everyone has to contribute,” he said, adding that the team no longer has a player who opens a match with a flash of genius, but can do many things together, even if Messi is irreplaceable.



Then he turned to his own situation, giving a very positive hint about his future with the national team. “If all goes well, I will continue as coach,” Scaloni explained before adding that “Messi’s legacy is the biggest example we can take.”



Scaloni’s contract expires in December 2026, and although he casted doubt on his future after the World Cup, he has since opened direct negotiations with AFA president Claudio “Chiqui” Tapia to extend his deal through the next World Cup.



Lionel Scaloni with the World Cup trophy. (Getty Images)



The talks are advanced and could be settled in the coming weeks, with the reported plan being for him to stay until the end of 2030, a deal that would allow him to coach his third World Cup, after Qatar 2022 and North America 2026.


        


What’s next for Argentina



Argentina’s next matches will come in the November FIFA window, which runs from November 9 to 17, with a maximum of two games per team, marking the first time the national team plays without Messi in the squad.



The AFA has not yet announced opponents or venues, although one latent possibility is the long-delayed tour of Asia, which was originally planned for this window but was postponed so Messi’s farewell could take place in Argentina.



The road to the 2030 World Cup looks different for Argentina than for most teams. As one of the three countries that will host centenary games, together with Uruguay and Paraguay, Argentina has an automatic berth in the tournament, which means the team will not have to go through the usual qualifying process.



CONMEBOL has not yet announced how it will decide the rest of its entrants, since it is still waiting to learn whether FIFA will accept its proposal to expand the World Cup to 64 teams, so the format of the South American qualifiers remains unclear.

items.title: FIFA ranking: Argentina stays steady after Messi’s farewell, Portugal climbs two spots amid Cristiano Ronaldo turmoil
items.description:
Argentina holds second place in the latest FIFA ranking after Lionel Messi's farewell, while Portugal climbs two spots to fifth despite the turmoil around Cristiano Ronaldo. 
It has been a week full of emotion in the international game. Lionel Messi said goodbye to the Argentina national team in a special week for the Albiceleste, while Cristiano Ronaldo went through a controversy with Portugal that has dominated the headlines.



Against that backdrop, the latest FIFA ranking was released on Wednesday, October 7, and it shows how both national teams stand after the international break.



Spain stayed at the top with 2,011.57 points after a strong run in the UEFA Nations League. Argentina held steady in second place with 1,972.80 after winning all three of their friendly matches, followed by France with 1,958.86 and England with 1,925.59. It is the first ranking update since the World Cup, and it follows the window that ran from late September into early October.



The biggest movement inside the top 10 came from Portugal. Despite the turmoil around Ronaldo, who left the national team’s camp after the team’s first two matches of the window, Portugal rose from seventh to fifth, with 1,807.69 points, moving ahead of Brazil, now sixth with 1,806.51, and Morocco, seventh with 1,805.34.




Portugal on the march in October’s FIFA/Coca-Cola Men’s World Ranking 🇵🇹Read more: https://t.co/9mg60TOyjC pic.twitter.com/drw5GYcMMs— FIFA (@FIFAcom) October 7, 2026




FIFA ranking: Full top 10



Belgium, the Netherlands, and Mexico complete the top 10, with no changes in their positions. The next official FIFA ranking will be published on November 18, after Portugal’s final two group games in the Nations League, against Denmark on November 14 and Wales later that month.


        


RankTeamPoints1Spain2,011.572Argentina1,972.803France1,958.864England1,925.595Portugal1,807.696Brazil1,806.517Morocco1,805.348Belgium1,779.179Netherlands1,778.6110Mexico1,738.48



The latest ranking leaves Argentina in a strong position as it begins a new chapter without Messi, still second in the world and behind only Spain. Portugal, for its part, climbs to fifth in the middle of the most turbulent week of Ronaldo’s international career, though the margin over Brazil and Morocco is slim enough that a few results in November could reshuffle that part of the table.

items.title: Video: Lionel Messi scores 126th goal with Argentina in international farewell match vs Benin
items.description:
In the 68th minute of his farewell match against Benin, Lionel Messi scored his 126th international goal for La Albiceleste. 
In his international farewell match against Benin, Lionel Messi added another storybook chapter to his iconic career by scoring his 126th goal for Argentina in the 68th minute.



Following a foul on Agustín Giay inside the box, the referee awarded a penalty to Argentina, and the packed crowd at the Estadio Monumental instantly knew who would step up to take it.



Lionel Messi immediately grabbed the ball, placed it on the penalty spot, and calmly slotted his shot home to score Argentina’s third goal of the night and his 126th overall with the national team.




GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOAL MESSSSSSSSSSSSSI 🐐🐐🐐🐐💔هذه المباراة برعاية @LOJASTOREGT pic.twitter.com/AONIp78FA8— Messi World (@M10GOAT) October 7, 2026




A much-needed goal



On the night Lionel Messi said goodbye to the Argentina national team, everyone inside the Estadio Monumental was eagerly awaiting a goal from their captain.



Even though it ultimately arrived from a penalty kick, Lionel Messi attempted to score in various ways throughout the entire match, whether shooting from outside the box or making clever runs behind defenders to push the ball past the goalkeeper.


        


Messi had already been directly involved in the night’s first two goals, assisting both Nicolás Otamendi and Nico Paz for their respective strikes. However, scoring a goal of his own was deeply desired both by him and by the passionate crowd packed into River Plate’s iconic stadium.



Is Lionel Messi completely retiring from international soccer?



Yes, Lionel Messi will no longer play for Argentina. He reached this final decision after the 2026 World Cup final defeat against Spain, having already conquered every major trophy with the national team.



Lionel Messi remains an active professional player for Inter Miami, which technically keeps him eligible for future national team call-ups. However, this departure feels vastly different from his brief 2016 retirement attempt, making the end of his international career all but definitive.

items.title: Video: Lionel Messi in tears during Argentina’s national anthem in international farewell match
items.description:
Lionel Messi was moved to tears during Argentina's national anthem just before his farewell match against Benin at the Monumental. 
Lionel Messi could not hold back the tears at the Monumental in Buenos Aires. The Argentina captain broke down toward the end of the national anthem, just minutes before the start of his farewell match against Benin, in front of a stadium that came to say goodbye to its greatest idol.



The anthem was performed by singer Fabio Santana, a Islas Malvinas (Falkland Islands) veteran, and Messi sang along with his children and a crowd that was moved to tears as well. 



It was the last time he heard it as a player for the national team, and the emotion overflowed when the final verses were reaching their end. Earlier in the day, Messi had already been seen wiping away tears on the way to the stadium.



Messi is playing his 208th and final match for Argentina after 21 years with the national team, in which he scored 125 goals, won the 2022 World Cup, the 2022 Finalissima and the Copa América twice, and became the most-capped player in its history.



الاسطورة يذرف الدموع 💔💔💔 https://t.co/eg7OOfmRcD— Messi World (@M10GOAT) October 6, 2026




The next question: who inherits the No. 10?



Messi’s farewell also opens one of the most symbolic debates in Argentine soccer: who will wear the No. 10 after him. Coach Lionel Scaloni has said the shirt will not be handed to anyone right away, and that it will stay reserved until after the match against Benin.


        


According to TyC Sports, Nicolás Paz and Franco Mastantuono are the main candidates. Other names being discussed include Alexis Mac Allister, Enzo Fernández and Thiago Almada, while ESPN Argentina’s Federico Bueno reports that the team has an internal plan for Paz to inherit it if Scaloni renews his contract, which expires on December 31.



Retiring the number, as AFA president Claudio Tapia once promised, is not an option in official tournaments. FIFA requires World Cup and Copa América squads to use consecutive numbers from 1 to 26, so Argentina cannot leave the No. 10 empty, a rule that already blocked an attempt to retire Diego Maradona’s shirt before the 2002 World Cup.

items.title: Who is the new captain of Argentina national team after the retirement of Lionel Messi?
items.description:
With Lionel Messi bidding farewell to Argentina on Tuesday, coach Lionel Scaloni has confirmed Cristian "Cuti" Romero as the new captain. 
Lionel Messi will say goodbye to the Argentina national team on Tuesday, October 6, in a farewell friendly against Benin at the Monumental in Buenos Aires, closing a 21-year international career. 



His departure leaves much more than a gap in attack: Messi has worn the captain’s armband since 2011, through the Copa América titles, the Finalissima, and the 2022 and 2026 World Cups, so Argentina needs a new leader to take it from here.



That leader is Cristian “Cuti” Romero. Coach Lionel Scaloni confirmed in late September that the 28-year-old Atlético Madrid defender will inherit the armband once Messi plays his last match, ending the speculation over who would take on one of the most demanding roles in world soccer.



Scaloni explained the choice with a simple argument: Romero was already Argentina’s third captain, behind Messi and Nicolás Otamendi, who also retired from international duty after the World Cup. 



Cristian Romero celebrates after scoring against Bolivia, wearing the captain’s armband. (Getty Images)



“Cuti is the right one,” he said. The coach also named Emiliano Martínez, Rodrigo De Paul and Lautaro Martínez as players who can wear the armband when needed, a sign that the leadership group is being rebuilt around the core of the 2022 champions.


        


Romero was not new to the role. He had captained Argentina three times before the announcement: in a 1-0 win over Chile in 2025 World Cup qualifying, in a friendly against Venezuela that October, and in a 2-1 win over Mauritania before the 2026 World Cup. His first match as the official captain came against Bolivia in Cordoba, his hometown, where Argentina won 4-0 and Romero scored the third goal with a header.



The defender who became a leader



Romero said that coming back to the stadium where he began his career with Belgrano ten years ago, now wearing the armband, was something he never imagined, and that he feels ready for the responsibility.



He has made 59 appearances for Argentina and scored five goals, all with his head, which makes him a constant threat from set pieces. He was part of the teams that won the 2021 Copa América, the 2022 Finalissima, the 2022 World Cup and the 2024 Copa América.



After starting his career at Belgrano, Romero moved to Italy, where he played for Genoa and Atalanta. In 2021 he joined Tottenham, where he established himself as a leader of the team, and this season he moved to Atlético Madrid for a reported 40 million euros, at the explicit request of Diego Simeone.



On Tuesday, Messi will play his last match as Argentina’s captain, and he is set to formally hand the armband to Romero in front of almost 90,000 fans at the Monumental. Romero has said no one will replace Messi, but that the team has to move forward and take Argentina back to the top, with the first chapter of the post-Messi era already under way.

items.title: Harry Kane joins Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo in exclusive list after scoring his 90th goal for England
items.description:
Harry Kane has reached 90 goals for England, joining Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo in a very small group of players to hit that mark at international level. 
Harry Kane has reached 90 goals for England, joining Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo in a very small group of players to hit that mark at international level. The England captain got there against Czechia at Wembley, in Matchday 4 of the UEFA Nations League.



Kane scored in the 40th minute, collecting a lofted cross from Morgan Rogers and finishing low into the bottom left corner to make it 2-0 before halftime. England had taken the lead through a Vladimír Coufal own goal in the 25th minute, which came after a cross from Kane himself.



As if that weren’t enough for the captain, he added another goal after the break to make it 3-0 at Wembley, reaching 91 for England. He had already made history before halftime, when he extended his team’s lead.



Only seven players have scored 90 goals for their national teams: Ali Daei, Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi, Sunil Chhetri, Romelu Lukaku, Robert Lewandowski and now Kane.




Staggering 🤯 pic.twitter.com/6ZRO7P4cws— England (@England) October 6, 2026




Ronaldo leads the list with 146 goals for Portugal, Messi, who plays his farewell match for Argentina tonight, follows in second place with 125, while Daei rounds out the podium with 108 goals.


        


A historic night for Kane



The goals were not the only milestone for Kane at Wembley. The England captain made his 125th appearance for the Three Lions, matching goalkeeper Peter Shilton’s all-time record for the men’s national team. Shilton’s mark had stood since 1990.



Kane had already passed Wayne Rooney during the 2026 World Cup as England’s most-capped outfield player, and he is also the team’s all-time leading scorer. He is set to break Shilton’s record next month, when England face Croatia in Matchday 5 of the Nations League.



These marks add to a historic England career for Kane, who is the Three Lions’ all-time leading scorer, 38 goals ahead of second-placed Wayne Rooney. He also holds the national team’s World Cup scoring record with 14 goals, four more than Gary Lineker, and has scored seven times at the European Championship, a tally he shares with Alan Shearer.

items.title: Argentina bids Messi farewell in final national team match, ending an era
How many titles did Lionel Messi win with Argentina?
items.description:
Rising from the ashes of early heartbreak to become the immortal captain of a golden generation, the maestro leaves behind a glittering empire of shattered records and ultimate glory, a breathtaking legacy that echoes into eternity. 
The final sun sets on the greatest era in Argentine soccer. Lionel Messi prepares for one last, deeply emotional dance upon the hallowed turf of the Estadio Monumental against Benin, drawing the curtain on a legendary 21-year international odyssey. Rising from the ashes of early heartbreak to become the immortal captain of a golden generation, the maestro leaves behind a glittering empire of shattered records and ultimate glory, a breathtaking legacy that echoes into eternity.



The 39-year-old will wear the famous blue and white shirt for the final time when Argentina faces Benin in Buenos Aires. The match is expected to be an emotional celebration for a player who has represented his country since making his senior debut in 2005. Messi has already confirmed that his international career is coming to an end, leaving the Monumental as the setting for his final chapter. 



“The moment has arrived. I leave in peace, I gave it my all. This shirt was my dream, my pride, and my life,” Messi said in a message shared by Adidas Football.  He also thanked the supporters who followed him through the difficult years as well as the unforgettable successes. “Thank you for loving me so much. I will always carry you with me,” the 39-year-old added.



Leo: "thank you for loving me so much" us: 🥹🥹🥹🥹🥹🥹🥹🥹🥹🥹 pic.twitter.com/fx2Zffq1er— adidas Football (@adidasfootball) October 6, 2026 



From painful defeats to era of dominance



Messi’s Argentina career did not begin with the success that eventually defined it. When he made his debut, Argentina had not won a senior international trophy since the 1993 Copa America, while Messi himself would experience several heartbreaking defeats before finally changing the story.



Lionel Messi of Argentina takes his medal off after during the 2014 FIFA World Cup



Argentina lost the 2007 Copa America final, the 2014 World Cup final and the 2015 and 2016 Copa America finals. After the 2016 defeat to Chile, Messi even announced his international retirement before reversing his decision weeks later.



The breakthrough finally arrived in 2021, when Argentina defeated Brazil 1-0 at the Maracanã to win the Copa America. That victory opened the door to the most successful period of Messi’s international career and removed the biggest criticism that had followed him for years.



Angel Di Maria, Lionel Messi and Nicolas Otamendi of Argentina celebrate with the trophy after the team’s victory in the CONMEBOL Copa America 2024



How many titles did Messi win with Argentina?



Messi won six titles representing Argentina across senior, youth, and Olympic competitions. Four of those came with the senior national team, while the other two arrived earlier in his career. His six titles are the 2005 FIFA U-20 World Cup, 2008 Olympic gold medal, 2021 Copa America, 2022 Finalissima, 2022 FIFA World Cup and 2024 Copa America.



The first came at the 2005 FIFA U-20 World Cup, where Messi scored six goals and won both the Golden Boot and Golden Ball. Three years later, he was part of the Argentina squad that won Olympic gold in Beijing after defeating Nigeria in the final.



YearTournamentOpponent in FinalMatch Result2005FIFA U-20 World CupNigeria2–12008Beijing Olympic Games (Gold Medal)Nigeria1–0



His senior breakthrough came in 2021, when Argentina ended a 28-year wait for a major senior trophy by beating Brazil in the Copa America final. Messi then added the 2022 Finalissima, before reaching the pinnacle of his international career later that year.



At the 2022 FIFA World Cup, Argentina defeated France in a dramatic final that ended 3-3 after extra time before winning on penalties. Messi scored twice, converted his penalty in the shootout, and finally lifted the trophy that had eluded him for so long.



YearTournamentOpponent in FinalMatch Result2021Copa AmericaBrazil1–02022CONMEBOL–UEFA Cup of Champions (Finalissima)Italy3–02022FIFA World CupFrance3–3 (4–2 pens)2024Copa AméricaColombia1–0 (a.e.t.)



His final senior title arrived at the 2024 Copa America, when Argentina defeated Colombia 1-0 after extra time. Lautaro Martínez scored the decisive goal, allowing Messi and Argentina to celebrate another continental championship.

In the last international game of Lionel Messi, Argentina faces Benin in an international friendly. Here is all the information on how to watch Messi's farewell match live in the United States. 
Here are all of the details of where you can watch Argentina vs Benin on US television and via legal streaming:



WHO: Argentina vs BeninWHAT: 2026 International friendlyWHEN: 7:00 PM ET / 4:00 PM PT • Tuesday, October 6, 2026WHERE: ViX



Match Overview



The world tunes in for a historic moment as Lionel Messi, an icon of the sport, plays his final match for Argentina. This international friendly is more than just a game; it’s a coronation and a farewell ceremony for the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner. La Albiceleste enters this match on a formidable run, having dominated African opposition since late 2025, and their only recent blemish is a hard-fought extra-time loss to Spain in the World Cup final. The atmosphere in Buenos Aires will be electric as the nation prepares to honor its greatest-ever player.



For Benin, the challenge is monumental. Ranked 93rd in the world, they step into the role of opposition for this momentous occasion. While they have been resilient recently, losing just one of their last five matches, they face a colossal gap in quality against the world champions. The stakes for Argentina are purely emotional—to provide a spectacular send-off for a legend. For Benin, it’s an opportunity to test themselves against the best and play a part in football history, even if the odds are overwhelmingly stacked against them.



Tactical Analysis & Match Context



Argentina comes into this match in scintillating form, having secured dominant friendly victories over Bolivia (4-0) and Burkina Faso’s U-23 side (7-0). These games have served as a perfect warm-up, allowing manager Lionel Scaloni to showcase his team’s offensive firepower while building momentum. The focus is twofold: celebrating Messi’s unparalleled career and integrating the next generation of talent that will carry the torch forward. This match represents the closing of one chapter and the beginning of another for the South American giants.



Benin’s journey has been one of resilience and near misses, having narrowly been edged out of World Cup qualification on goal difference. Their tactical approach against a powerhouse like Argentina will undoubtedly be pragmatic and defensive. Expect them to deploy a low block, absorb pressure, and look for rare opportunities on the counter-attack. The tactical battle will be waged entirely in Benin’s half, with Argentina expected to dominate possession and relentlessly probe for openings. The key for Argentina will be breaking down a packed defense, a task made easier by their world-class attacking talent.



The primary motivation for every player in an Argentina shirt will be to ensure Lionel Messi’s final international appearance is a memorable one, filled with goals and celebration. For Benin, the objective is to deliver a disciplined and respectable performance on a global stage. However, their preparations have been marred by controversy, including complaints about travel arrangements and accommodations, which could impact their mental and physical readiness for such a demanding fixture.



Head-to-Head Record & Historic Trends



This international friendly marks the first-ever meeting between Argentina and Benin. With no historical data to draw from, the context of this matchup is defined entirely by the current form and status of the two nations. The clash at the Estadio Monumental is designed as a tribute to Lionel Messi, and the opposition was chosen to ensure a celebratory atmosphere.



While there is no direct history, Argentina’s recent record against African teams provides a clear indication of what to expect. Since November 2025, they have won all eight of their matches against African opponents, boasting an incredible aggregate score of 29-4. This trend of dominance underscores the significant gap in quality and resources between the two sides.



Statistically, Argentina is an offensive juggernaut. They have averaged 2.76 goals per game over their last 17 matches. In the three games during 2026 where their odds were overwhelmingly short (priced below 1.10), they scored a staggering 16 goals combined. With the entire team focused on creating chances for Messi in his farewell, expect Argentina to generate a high volume of shots and scoring opportunities.



Squad News & Projected Lineups



Argentina enters the match with a nearly full-strength squad, poised to deliver a fitting tribute, though they will be missing a few key players. Benin arrives with a complete roster, ready to face the daunting task ahead despite a challenging journey to South America.



Manager Lionel Scaloni will have to make do without the injured trio of Giovani Lo Celso, Thiago Almada, and Nicolás Tagliafico. However, their absences open the door for rising stars like Benfica’s Gianluca Prestianni and Real Madrid’s Nico Paz to feature, signaling a bright future for the national team. The focus, however, remains squarely on building the attack around Messi for his final bow.



Benin’s preparations have been far from ideal, with reports of player fatigue and dissatisfaction over travel logistics. Despite these off-field issues, coach Gernot Rohr has his full complement of players available. They are expected to field their strongest possible lineup in an attempt to contain the relentless Argentine attack and maintain defensive solidity.



Argentina Projected XI (4-4-2): E. Martínez; Giay, Romero, Martínez, Medina; Prestianni, Fernández, Mac Allister, Paz; Messi, Álvarez.



This attacking formation is designed to maximize possession and create constant pressure. With Enzo Fernández and Alexis Mac Allister controlling the midfield, the forwards—spearheaded by the legendary Messi and the tireless Julián Álvarez—will have ample service to dismantle Benin’s defense.

items.title: Why is Bukayo Saka not playing for England vs Czechia in Matchday 4 of the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League?
items.description:
Bukayo Saka has been left out of England's starting lineup for Tuesday's Nations League clash with Czechia at Wembley, with Thomas Tuchel opting to rotate his squad for the final match of the international break. The Arsenal winger's absence from the XI comes just three days after he scored twice in England's historic 7-0 rout […] 
Bukayo Saka has been left out of England‘s starting lineup for Tuesday’s Nations League clash with Czechia at Wembley, with Thomas Tuchel opting to rotate his squad for the final match of the international break.



The Arsenal winger’s absence from the XI comes just three days after he scored twice in England’s historic 7-0 rout of Croatia, and no injury concerns have been reported for him.



Instead, the decision appears to be one of rotation, with Tuchel having said that his starting side would be “a mix” of players who started and those who came off the bench against Croatia.



In Saka‘s place, Morgan Rogers and Eberechi Eze join captain Harry Kane in England’s attacking trio, while Jude Bellingham retains his spot at the starting XI in midfield alongside Elliot Anderson and Myles Lewis-Skelly.




A truly remarkable milestone 👑Harry Kane is set to level Peter Shilton’s record for the most #ThreeLions caps of all-time. pic.twitter.com/rgwzZpp3gO— England (@England) October 6, 2026




England enters the match second in Group A3 of League A behind Spain, having won its last two games without conceding a goal, and will look to close out this international window on the best possible note. Kane, meanwhile, is set to equal Peter Shilton’s all-time record of 125 England caps with his appearance against the Czechs.


        


Confirmed lineup for England



Tuchel’s confirmed XI features several changes from the side that thrashed Croatia, with Bukayo Saka among the players rested after his brace on Saturday. 



Jude Bellingham, who scored in that win, retains his place in midfield alongside Elliot Anderson and Myles Lewis-Skelly, while Morgan Rogers and Eberechi Eze support Harry Kane up front. Trent Alexander-Arnold takes the right-back spot, with Alex Scott and Ezri Konsa both unavailable through injury.



England confirmed starting XI: Jordan Pickford; Trent Alexander-Arnold, Jarell Quansah, Marc Guéhi, Lewis Hall; Elliot Anderson, Jude Bellingham, Myles Lewis-Skelly; Morgan Rogers, Harry Kane (C), Eberechi Eze.

items.title: Is Lionel Messi retiring from Inter Miami following his Argentina departure?
items.description:
Lionel Messi is retiring from international soccer following his farewell with the Argentina national team, but is his Inter Miami career also over? 
Lionel Messi has decided to put an end to his international career. Now that he has retired from Argentina, the biggest question is what will happen with his career at Inter Miami?



Following the 2026 World Cup, Lionel Messi announced that his time with Argentina had come to an end. The final defeat against Spain solidified his decision to step away from the national team.



Nevertheless, his announcement applied solely to the Argentina national team. Lionel Messi will not retire from soccer entirely, as he intends to fulfill his signed contract with Inter Miami, which runs through December 2028.



Will Lionel Messi retire after his Inter Miami run?



Lionel Messi’s current contract extension with Inter Miami runs through December 2028. By that time, he will be 41 years old, and his long-term future remains uncertain.



Lionel Messi of Argentina celebrates after scoring. (Hernan Cortez/Getty Images)



With his international retirement confirmed, it appears unlikely that Messi will play far beyond 2028. Barcelona supporters hold onto hope for an emotional return, though any homecoming would likely have to occur prior to the conclusion of his Inter Miami deal via a short-term loan.


        


While Messi could theoretically continue playing past 2028 or sign a short stint with Barcelona to retire at the club where he became a legend, his immediate focus remains centered on his ongoing tenure in Major League Soccer.



Could Lionel Messi still return to Argentina after his retirement?



Yes. As long as he remains an active professional player, Lionel Messi remains eligible to represent the Argentina national team should he reconsider his decision and receive a call-up from the coaching staff.



In 2016, Messi famously announced his initial retirement from international duty before reversing the decision after further reflection—ultimately returning to lead La Albiceleste to historic world and continental glory.

items.title: Why is Kylian Mbappe not playing for France vs Belgium in 2026-27 UEFA Nations League Matchday 4?
items.description:
France host Belgium at the Stade de France in a pivotal Matchday 4 encounter in Group A1 of the 2026–27 UEFA Nations League, but Les Bleus will be without captain and star forward Kylian Mbappe. 
The opening window of the 2026–27 UEFA Nations League is drawing to a close. On Matchday 4, France host Belgium, but Les Bleus will be without star forward Kylian Mbappe for this marquee fixture.



During France’s 1–0 victory over Turkiye on foreign soil, Mbappe suffered a hyperextension of his left knee shortly after scoring the winning goal. He was substituted immediately following the incident.



Following medical evaluation, the French Football Federation confirmed he would return to Spain to recover and prepare for Real Madrid’s upcoming fixtures, ruling him out for the remainder of this international break.



Who will replace Kylian Mbappe against Belgium?



In their previous outing against Italy, head coach Zinedine Zidane deployed Desire Doue on the wing and moved Ousmane Dembele into a central attacking role, with Michael Olise completing the front line.



Kylian Mbappe #10 of France.



While Mbappe offers unmatched power and dynamic scoring, the attacking trident of Olise, Dembele, and Doue remains a formidable threat for any opponent. Against Belgium, France require a victory to secure top spot in Group A1.


        


Fortunately, Mbappe’s injury is not believed to be severe. Having already returned to Madrid, the forward is expected to be fit in time for Real Madrid’s La Liga clash against Villarreal on October 10.

items.title: Ronaldo’s break with Portugal is sad, fitting, and long overdue | Jonathan Wilson
items.description: The star’s rift with Jorge Jesus is an unfortunate affair. But the forward has been holding his national team back for yearsSign up for our free newsletter hereIf this is to be the end for Cristiano Ronaldo at international level, at least it can be said that he left the stage as he bestrode it: with monumental self-regard. Ronaldo has always been a preening, self-absorbed player, but for a time, when he was one of the best in the world, it could be tolerated. For the past four years, though, he has actively and obviously held Portugal back. There is a great generation of technical talent here weighed down by the monstrous albatross of his ego.To recap the basic details of the past couple of weeks. Ronaldo played 67 minutes of Portugal’s scratchy 1-0 win over Wales. Portugal coach Jorge Jesus, who replaced Roberto Martínez after the World Cup, said he had a verbal agreement with Ronaldo that he would not start the following game against Norway but would perhaps come off the bench. Early in the second half, Ronaldo went to warm up – although whether that was on his own initiative or because Jesus had told him to is unclear. The game was tight, Portugal ultimately winning 2-1, and Jesus did not bring Ronaldo on. Continue reading...

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo farewell game: Portugal reportedly plan tribute as Jorge Jesus leaves door open for return
items.description:
Reports indicate that the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) is exploring options to organize a formal farewell match for Cristiano Ronaldo, while head coach Jorge Jesus is open for the captain's return to A Seleção. 
The Portugal national team saw Cristiano Ronaldo leave camp earlier this week. Now, reports have emerged that the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) is preparing a farewell match for the icon, and head coach Jorge Jesus remains open to his return.



At the start of the 2026–27 UEFA Nations League campaign, Cristiano Ronaldo departed the Portuguese squad following a reported disagreement with Jorge Jesus over the manager’s decision to leave him out of the starting lineup.



Now, according to L’Équipe, the Portuguese federation is planning a farewell match for Cristiano Ronaldo, allowing him to properly say goodbye to the fans and step away from international football with the honor his career deserves.



Would Jorge Jesus accept Cristiano Ronaldo’s return?



Following Ronaldo’s departure, many supporters anticipated severe consequences for Jorge Jesus, with some speculating he might be dismissed. However, the manager continues to deliver positive results on the pitch, making a coaching change highly unlikely.


        


According to A Bola, Jorge Jesus is open to having Ronaldo return to the squad for a proper farewell match. The manager has publicly praised the striker on multiple occasions, framing the situation as a miscommunication rather than a personal rift.



Jorge Jesus coach of Portugal



Nevertheless, questions linger over whether Ronaldo would agree to return with Jorge Jesus at the helm. Their relationship remains visibly strained, and the legendary forward may resist playing under the manager following their recent friction.



All eyes set on the 1,000th goal mark



With Ronaldo potentially returning only for a ceremonial farewell fixture, the end of his playing career draws near. The forward had previously indicated that the current season with Al Nassr could be his last in professional soccer.



While lifting the 2026–27 UEFA Nations League trophy was initially his primary objective this season, his focus now shifts toward reaching 1,000 official career goals—a historic milestone no player in football history has ever achieved.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s controversial departure prompts Bruno Fernandes to call for unity in Portugal
items.description:
Bruno Fernandes broke his silence on Cristiano Ronaldo's dramatic Portugal exit, calling for unity and insisting the squad remains unaffected by the controversy swirling around his former captain. 
Bruno Fernandes addressed the fallout from Cristiano Ronaldo‘s controversial exit from Portugal’s training camp for the first time on Saturday, calling on the country to stay united rather than take sides in the ongoing saga.



Speaking to reporters, Fernandes revealed he had spoken with Ronaldo directly and said he intended to repeat publicly what he told him privately: that regardless of how the situation unfolds, Ronaldo remains an irreplaceable figure for the national team and the country as a whole.



“Cris will never stop being the greatest symbol of our national team, the greatest symbol of our football and, probably, no, certainly, the greatest symbol of our country because of everything he has done, not only in Portugal but around the world,” he explained.



Fernandes, who has taken over the captain’s armband in Ronaldo’s absence, pushed back against the idea that the squad has been affected by the controversy, insisting the players remain focused and removed from the noise surrounding their former captain.




Por Portugal. 🇵🇹For Portugal. 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/uLKCufMaXA— Portugal (@selecaoportugal) October 3, 2026




He closed by urging fans not to pick sides. “The country should not divide itself, that people should not take sides, and that we should experience all of this as one,” Fernandes said. “Cris is and will always be the greatest icon of our national team, our football and also world football. He deserves the respect of all Portuguese people, regardless of who likes him more or likes him less“.


        


Fernandes insists the squad is unaffected



Beyond his comments on Ronaldo’s standing within the national team, Fernandes also pushed back against the idea that the controversy has seeped into the squad’s day-to-day atmosphere, insisting the players have largely tuned out the noise surrounding their former captain.



“We are completely outside the matter. We are aware of what you are saying and what we are seeing,” Fernandes said. “Honestly, we spend a lot of time in the players’ room playing cards rather than watching television, so we are very removed from all the controversy surrounding this matter“. He added that he believes “every household should resolve its affairs behind closed doors,” and that he’s confident the situation will eventually be resolved “for both sides.”



Fernandes’ comments come as Portugal tries to move past the saga on the pitch, having won both matches since Ronaldo was left out of the starting XI — against Norway, when he remained an unused substitute, and then against Denmark, by which point he had already left the squad entirely.



With the captain’s armband now his to keep for the foreseeable future, Fernandes finds himself in the position of both leading the team through a turbulent stretch and managing the public narrative around his predecessor, a dynamic that looks set to continue at least until Jesus addresses the situation in full after Sunday’s match against Norway.

items.title: Argentina-Burkina Faso friendly reportedly takes bizarre twist as African side set to present U-23 team
items.description:
Argentina's friendly against Burkina Faso took a bizarre turn hours before kickoff, with reports indicating the Albiceleste will face the African side's U-23 squad instead. 
Argentina‘s friendly against Burkina Faso has taken an unexpected turn just hours before kickoff, with reports indicating the Albiceleste will actually face Burkina Faso’s U-23 side rather than its senior squad.



The development was confirmed by Burkina Faso insider Romain Molina, who had previously reported that several first-team players planned to skip the trip to Buenos Aires in protest.



He later revealed that only one member of Burkina Faso’s senior squad ultimately boarded the flight, with the rest opting to stay behind in Africa after yet another delay to their charter flight proved to be the final straw.



According to Molina, Burkina Faso’s federation called up its U-23 squad, whose match against Mali had been canceled, in order to avoid an outright no-show. “The flight from Casablanca had to depart late and will only arrive around 15:30 local time in Buenos Aires to play at 21:00. Shameful from start to finish,” Molina wrote on X.




La Selección Argentina vuelve al Monumental para reencontrarse con uno de los escenarios más importantes de su historia.🏟️ https://t.co/Dm4mpNjZn5 pic.twitter.com/nxjRQ1inNw— 🇦🇷 Selección Argentina ⭐⭐⭐ (@Argentina) October 3, 2026




The switch leaves Argentina facing an even greater mismatch than expected, with Burkina Faso missing key figures such as Edmond Tapsoba (Bayer Leverkusen), Arsène Kouassi (Lorient), Nasser Djiga (Wolverhampton) and Lassina Traoré (Shakhtar) for a friendly that was meant to showcase the senior national team.


        


Logistics company breaks silence on the situation



Eurodata Sport, the company responsible for organizing Burkina Faso’s travel logistics, released a statement from its founder, Jairo Pachón, addressing the situation. The statement emphasized that the only real issue was the cancellation of the original flight due to a technical fault with the aircraft, clearing both federations of blame.



The company also confirmed Romain Molina’s earlier reporting that several senior players had refused to travel. “Representatives from the Burkina Faso Football Federation and the government held several meetings with these players to ask them to reconsider their position and honor the commitment made with the AFA. However, despite these efforts, the players who had expressed their refusal maintained their decision,” the statement read.

items.title: Lamine Yamal starts today: Confirmed lineups for Spain vs Czechia in Matchday 3 of the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League
items.description:
Lamine Yamal looks to keep his hot streak going as Spain chases a third straight win, this time against a struggling Czech Republic side still searching for its first point. 
Spain hosts Czech Republic at the Estadio Nuevo Carlos Tartiere, looking to make it three wins from three in the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League as Lamine Yamal continues his sensational run of form.



La Roja opened the campaign with a 3-2 win over England at Wembley before thrashing Croatia 4-1 three days later, moving to six points and the top of Group 3 of League A. 



The reigning world and European champions have now won nine straight games in all competitions and remain unbeaten over 90 minutes since a friendly against Colombia back in March 2024.



Czech Republic, meanwhile, sit bottom of the group without a point, having lost 2-1 to Croatia in their opener before falling 2-0 at home to England. Santi Denia’s side are already under pressure heading into this one, and they’ve never beaten Spain in seven previous meetings, with La Roja winning five of those and the most recent encounter, in June 2022, ending in a 2-0 Spain victory.




𝗘𝘀𝗽𝗮𝗻̃𝗮 𝘃𝘂𝗲𝗹𝘃𝗲 𝗮 𝗢𝘃𝗶𝗲𝗱𝗼 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝗮 𝘀𝗲𝗴𝘂𝗶𝗿 𝘃𝗼𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗼.🏟️ Carlos Tartiere📌 Oviedo (Asturias)📺 @La1_tve La previa: https://t.co/VjUeDAH2bf#VamosEspaña | #NationsLeague pic.twitter.com/NyBAC3OYRh— Selección Española Masculina de Fútbol (@SEFutbol) October 3, 2026




Yamal has been nothing short of unstoppable this international window, with three goals and an assist in Spain’s first two matches, and he’s set to lead the line again as De la Fuente looks to extend his side’s dominant run.


        


Confirmed lineup for Spain



De la Fuente is expected to shuffle his side from the one that routed Croatia, with Aymeric Laporte poised to return to defense and Rodri and Dani Olmo both back in midfield.



Spain confirmed starting XI: David Raya; Iván Fresneda, Robin Le Normand, Aymeric Laporte, Fran García; Pedri, Rodri; Lamine Yamal, Dani Olmo, Alex Baena; Roberto Fernández.



Confirmed lineup for Czech Republic



Denia’s confirmed XI brought a few changes from the projection, with Antonín Kinský starting in goal ahead of Matěj Kovář and Robin Hranáč left out of the back line entirely.



Czech Republic confirmed starting XI: Antonín Kinský; Michal Sáček, Štěpán Chaloupek, Ladislav Krejčí, Jiří Sláma; Lukáš Ambros, Roman Macek, Alex Král; Matej Radosta, Ondřej Lingr, Adam Hložek.

items.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future successRead the full updates on our class of 2021 here and hereIn 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series.We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well).The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players.The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. items.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individualsWhat makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature. My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career.After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
